tasks.short: Collect fines at the desk, book payments, review unpaid fines, send reminders, respond to complaints about fines, and record waivers.

steps.what: Patrons pay fines online in their account or at the self-service kiosk
Library technician collects fines at the desk
Library technician books cash payments in the system and the cash register
Library technician checks the week's reminder batch before it goes: each fine is still unpaid and not waived or disputed, patron and amount are right, and the text follows the policy
Library technician sends the reminders: as posted letters today, by one release of e-mails from the library system after the change
Library technician responds to complaints about fines
Library technician records fine waivers

tasks.design: Patrons pay fines online in their account or at the self-service kiosk, and payments post to the library system ({OTHER}) automatically, so fewer fines are taken and booked at the desk. Each week the technician reviews the list of unpaid fines; the technician checks the batch and releases it once as e-mails from the system instead of letters. Waivers are recorded with a reason code. Handling complaints stays with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fines were paid in cash at the desk, booked by hand and chased by letter.
tasks.enabler_now: Library systems take online payments and send scheduled notices.
tasks.human_edge: Waiving a fine for a family that is struggling.
tasks.altitude: The technician handles exceptions instead of cash.

evidence.claim: Library systems can take online payments and send scheduled notices.
Basic administration is kept seven years and must stay usable at an audit.

assumptions: Boundary: from the fine due to the waiver recorded; debt collection is outside.
Input contract: payment provider connected; fallback is cash.
Patrons pay online in about the time paying at the desk took; a little patron time is priced.
Waivers stay with the technician under the policy; recording one keeps 80 because a reason code replaces part of the written reason. Recording it in the library system is an ordinary save.

incremental.description: Library technician helps patrons with failed online payments.

approvals.approved_version: The week's reminder batch, with each patron, fine and amount exactly as checked by the technician in s3, sent once by e-mail from the library system to each patron's registered address; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patrons still pay cash at the desk (s1 75, s2 60) (26.0); high: most pay online or at the kiosk (39.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train volunteers and student assistants, schedule their shifts, supervise their work, and record training done.

steps.what: Library technician trains other staff, volunteers or student assistants
Volunteers and student assistants pick open shifts in the rostering app
Library technician schedules their work in a spreadsheet and e-mails it
Library technician supervises their work on the floor
Library technician records training done on paper

tasks.design: Volunteers and student assistants pick open shifts in a shared rostering app ({HCM}), so the technician fills only the gaps instead of building a spreadsheet and e-mailing it. The technician ticks training done on a skills checklist per volunteer instead of writing it out. Training and supervising stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shifts were planned in a spreadsheet and training kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Rostering apps let volunteers pick shifts.

reach.learn: Whether gaps in the roster fall.

evidence.claim: Rostering apps let volunteers pick open shifts.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new volunteer to training recorded; recruitment is outside.
Input contract: volunteers use the app; fallback is the spreadsheet.
Volunteers spend a little time picking shifts; priced as other-role time.
Training and supervision keep their full time. s2 keeps 40 for filling gaps. s4 keeps 80: the checklist lists the skills, but recording each one stays a first record.

incremental.description: Library technician answers volunteers' questions about the rostering app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of volunteers do not use the app, so the technician still schedules them by hand (s2 70) (7.5); high: most pick their own shifts (13.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the reference question, search databases and printed sources, check references the patron brings, and give the answer.

steps.what: Library technician takes the patron's reference question
Library technician conducts reference searches using in-house and online databases

loop.input: The question and the library's catalogue and licensed databases.
loop.output: A short answer with links to the sources it used.
loop.check: Code drops any citation that does not resolve to a catalogue record or DOI. The technician reads each source before answering: does it answer the patron's question and say what the assistant claims; the assistant's text is not passed on unchecked, and unclear cases are searched by hand.
loop.stop: One search per question; if nothing resolves, the technician searches by hand and in printed materials.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patrons ask in their own words; keyword search misses sources described differently.

steps.what: Library technician checks whether references patrons bring exist
Library technician gives the answer to the patron

tasks.design: A research assistant in the discovery system ({OTHER}) answers from the catalogue and licensed databases with links, and code drops citations that do not resolve; the technician reads the sources before answering. A batch checker resolves the list of references a patron brings against catalogues and DOI registries and marks those that do not exist. Taking the question and answering the patron stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each question was searched by keyword, and doubtful references checked one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Discovery systems answer with links; DOI and catalogue lookups can be scripted.
tasks.still_hard: Patrons bring chatbot references to works that do not exist.
tasks.human_edge: Working out what a patron really wants to know.
tasks.altitude: The technician reviews sources instead of searching from scratch.

evidence.claim: Primo Research Assistant answers reference questions from the top five abstracts with source links.
The Library of Virginia estimates 15 percent of emailed reference questions are ChatGPT-generated, some citing invented works.
A reference chatbot must tell users it is AI; here the technician answers.

assumptions: Boundary: from the reference question to the answer given; interlibrary loans are outside.
Input contract: discovery system licensed; fallback is keyword search.
The technician reads sources before answering.
research_questions: How often does the check drop a citation?

already_counted.description: Library technician reads sources found by the assistant.

incremental.description: Library technician reports wrong results to the system manager.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: local history questions answered from print, so most searching and checking stay by hand (s2 85, s3 70) (10.7); high: questions answered from licensed databases (31.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Export usage data, combine and calculate figures, write the report commentary, check the report, send it to management, and submit figures to the national statistics.

steps.what: Library technician exports usage data from the library system
Library technician compiles data and calculates figures in spreadsheets
Library technician creates statistical reports on library usage with commentary
Library technician checks the final report: figures match the dashboard and the commentary says what the figures show
Library technician sends the report to management: by e-mail today, by one release from the dashboard after the change
Library technician checks the national figures before submitting: each count matches the dashboard and the national definitions
Library technician submits figures to the national library statistics

tasks.design: A usage dashboard ({BI}) reads loans, visits, events and digital use straight from the library systems and computes the standard figures, so data are not exported and combined in spreadsheets. The report template fills charts and tables for the period, and the technician writes the commentary. The technician checks the report and releases it once to management from the dashboard, then checks the national figures and submits them personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were exported from several systems and combined by hand each period.
tasks.still_hard: Visitor counters and event sign-ups sit in separate tools.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why loans fell in one branch.
tasks.altitude: The technician interprets figures instead of compiling them.

evidence.claim: Library systems can feed usage dashboards with loans, visits and digital use.
System logs that check staff output need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the reporting period to figures submitted; budget decisions are outside.
Input contract: systems connected to the dashboard; fallback is exports.
research_questions: Are reports ready sooner after period end?

incremental.description: Library technician adds counts from separate tools by hand.

approvals.approved_version: The report with its figures and commentary exactly as checked by the technician in s4, sent once from the dashboard to the management mailing list for this period; any change needs a new check.
The period's national figures exactly as checked by the technician in s5b, submitted once to the national library statistics portal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: several systems are not connected, so many figures are still exported and combined by hand (s1 60, s2 50) (39.0); high: all data reach the dashboard (59.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The library technician keeps answering patrons, handling complaints, training volunteers and interpreting figures; cash handling, spreadsheets and keyword searching shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time for readers.
